p.src: Now Chen Zongshan, having received the imperial edict, returned to his residence and made ready to depart. Many came to congratulate him, saying, “Grand Commandant, on this journey you will serve the state in the first place and ease the people’s burdens in the second. You will rid soldiers and civilians alike of this scourge. Loyalty and righteousness are the guiding principles at Liangshan Marsh, whose men merely await amnesty and enlistment from the court. You should speak kindly and persuasively to them and take particular care to soothe and reassure them.”

p.src: While they were still speaking, a steward from the Grand Preceptor’s residence arrived with an invitation: “The Grand Preceptor requests the Grand Commandant’s presence for a discussion.” Chen Zongshan mounted his sedan chair and went straight to the Grand Preceptor’s residence on New Song Gate Avenue. Alighting at the entrance, he was led by the steward directly into the study within the council hall. There he met the Grand Preceptor and took a seat to one side. When the tea had been served, Grand Preceptor Cai said, “I hear that the Son of Heaven has sent you to offer amnesty and enlistment to Liangshan Marsh. I summoned you especially to tell you this: once there, you must neither compromise the discipline of the imperial court nor disrupt the laws of the state. Have you not heard the Analects say: ‘In his conduct he has a sense of shame, and when sent to the four quarters he does not disgrace his ruler’s command—such a man may be called an envoy’?” Grand Commandant Chen replied, “I understand it all. I am grateful for Your Excellency’s instruction.” Cai Jing continued, “I shall have this steward accompany you. He is thoroughly versed in the rules and regulations. Should you overlook anything, he will call it to your attention.” Grand Commandant Chen said, “I am deeply grateful for Your Excellency’s generous consideration.” Taking leave of the Grand Preceptor, he led the steward out of the minister’s residence, mounted his sedan chair, and returned home.

p.src: He had barely settled down when the gatekeeper announced that Marshal Gao had dismounted outside. Grand Commandant Chen hurried out to welcome him, invited him into the hall, and seated him. After they had exchanged the customary courtesies, Grand Commandant Gao said, “When the court discussed offering amnesty and enlistment to Song Jiang today, had I, Gao Qiu, been present, I would certainly have stopped it. That bandit has repeatedly humiliated the imperial court, and his crimes cry out to Heaven. If these criminals are now pardoned and brought into the capital, they will surely become a future menace. I wished to remonstrate, but the imperial word had already been pronounced, so for now we must see how the matter proceeds. If those bandits remain blind to conscience and treat the sacred edict with contempt, you must return to the capital without delay. I shall report the matter to the Son of Heaven, muster a great army, and go there in person to cut down the weeds and tear out their roots. That is my dearest wish. For your journey, I have under my command an aide who is quick and fluent of speech, and can give ten answers to a single question. He will be well suited to advise you on affairs.” Grand Commandant Chen thanked him, saying, “I am most grateful for the Marshal’s thoughtful concern.” Gao Qiu rose to leave. Grand Commandant Chen escorted him to the entrance, where he mounted his horse and departed.

p.src: The next day, Administrative Officer Zhang from Grand Preceptor Cai’s residence and Aide Li from Marshal Gao’s residence both arrived. Grand Commandant Chen had the horses saddled and the members of the party mustered. The ten jars of imperial wine were placed in a dragon-and-phoenix carrying frame and borne beneath a yellow banner at the head of the procession. Grand Commandant Chen mounted his horse with five or six personal attendants. Administrative Officer Zhang and Aide Li were also mounted, while the vermilion edict was carried before them on a man’s back. Thus the company passed out through New Song Gate. The subordinate officials who had come to see them off then all turned back. They journeyed on until at length they reached Jizhou. Prefect Zhang Shuye received them and invited them into his residence, where he laid a banquet in their honor. When he asked about the proposed amnesty and enlistment, Grand Commandant Chen related every detail. Zhang Shuye said, “In my humble opinion, offering them amnesty and enlistment is the best course. There is only one consideration: when you arrive, Grand Commandant, you must maintain an air of goodwill, address the whole band with kind and persuasive words, and soothe them. Whether they prove good or bad, the important thing is to bring this great undertaking to completion. Several among them have tempers like blazing fire. Should a word or half a phrase give offense, the whole enterprise will be ruined.” Administrative Officer Zhang and Aide Li said, “With the two of us accompanying the Grand Commandant, nothing can possibly go amiss. Prefect, you keep urging caution and harmony, but that would only damage the imperial court’s discipline. Such low fellows must always be kept down and never allowed the least advantage. Let them raise their heads, and they will immediately put on airs.” Zhang Shuye asked, “Who are these two men?” Grand Commandant Chen replied, “This man is an administrative officer in Grand Preceptor Cai’s residence, and the other is an aide in Grand Commandant Gao’s residence.” Zhang Shuye said, “It would be better if these two officers did not go!” Grand Commandant Chen said, “They are trusted confidants of the Cai and Gao households. If I do not take them, their masters will certainly become suspicious.” Zhang Shuye said, “I spoke only in the hope of a successful outcome, for I fear your labors may prove fruitless.” Administrative Officer Zhang said, “With the two of us there, not a drop could leak through even ten thousand fathoms of water.” Zhang Shuye dared say no more. He arranged a banquet for their entertainment and afterward escorted them to the official hostel to rest. The next day, the authorities of Jizhou sent a messenger ahead to notify Liangshan Marsh.

p.src: Now Song Jiang met daily with the assembled company in the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness to discuss military affairs. A spy had already reported the news, though it had not yet been confirmed, and Song Jiang was delighted at heart. That day, a young retainer led the messenger from Jizhou straight into the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness. The man reported, “The imperial court has now dispatched a grand commandant named Chen Zongshan, bearing ten jars of imperial wine and a vermilion edict pardoning your crimes and offering amnesty and enlistment. He has already arrived within Jizhou city. You should make ready here to receive him.” Song Jiang was overjoyed. He gave the messenger food and wine, together with two bolts of colored satin and ten taels of fine silver, and sent him back ahead of them. Song Jiang said to the company, “Once we accept amnesty and enlistment, we shall become servants of the state, and all the hardships we have endured for so long will not have been in vain! Only today shall we attain our true reward!” Wu Yong laughed and said, “In my judgment, this attempt at amnesty and enlistment is certain to fail. Even if it succeeds, they will regard us as no more than weeds and chaff. Let those fellows first lead a great army against us. We shall deal them such cruel blows, killing their men and felling their horses, that the very thought of us will terrify them in their dreams. If we accept amnesty only then, we shall retain some dignity.” Song Jiang said, “If you speak in such a fashion, you will disgrace the two words ‘loyalty and righteousness.’” Lin Chong said, “When a high official comes from court, he will put on no end of airs. There may well be treachery hidden in this affair.” Guan Sheng said, “The edict is certain to contain threatening words intended to intimidate us.” Xu Ning added, “The envoy is certain to be one of Grand Commandant Gao’s men.” Song Jiang said, “Do not be suspicious. For now, attend only to making ready to receive the edict.” He first ordered Song Qing and Cao Zheng to prepare the banquet, placing Chai Jin in overall charge of arrangements and insisting that everything be perfectly orderly. They erected a reception pavilion for the Grand Commandant, displayed silk and satin in five colors, and adorned the hall both inside and out with colored hangings and flowers. Pei Xuan, Xiao Rang, Lü Fang, and Guo Sheng were sent down the mountain in advance to wait beside the road twenty li away and welcome the envoy. The naval commanders made ready great ships along the shore. Wu Yong passed down an order: “All of you must act exactly as I direct. Otherwise, this affair cannot proceed.”

p.src: Now Xiao Rang, leading his three companions and five or six attendants, went twenty li out to welcome them, carrying wine and fruit but not a single weapon. That day, as Grand Marshal Chen traveled along the road, Administrative Officer Zhang and Equerry Li walked before his horse rather than riding. No fewer than two or three hundred attendants followed behind. Some dozen mounted officers from Jizhou formed an escort at the front; the imperial wine was borne in dragon-and-phoenix carrying cases, while a mounted man carried the edict box on his back. There were also fifty or sixty Jizhou jailers in the procession, all eager to enter Liangshan Marsh in hopes of gaining some modest advancement. Xiao Rang, Pei Xuan, Lü Fang, and Guo Sheng met the party midway and prostrated themselves beside the road in welcome. Administrative Officer Zhang demanded, “Who does this Song Jiang imagine himself to be? The Emperor’s edict has arrived—why has he not come to receive it in person? This is outrageous contempt for the sovereign! You are all men who deserve death; how could you be worthy of the court’s amnesty? Grand Marshal, let us turn back!” Xiao Rang, Pei Xuan, Lü Fang, and Guo Sheng prostrated themselves on the ground and pleaded forgiveness: “Until now, no imperial edict has ever reached our stronghold, so we could not know whether the matter was genuine. Song Jiang and all the leaders, high and low, are waiting at Golden Sands Beach to welcome you. We earnestly beg Your Excellency to calm your thunderous anger, help bring this good service to the state to completion, and graciously forgive us.” Equerry Li said, “Even if we do not bring this good business to completion, we need not fear that you bandits will sprout wings and fly to heaven.” A poem bears witness:

p.src: At this, Lü Fang and Guo Sheng said, “What sort of talk is that! How dare they look down on us so!” Xiao Rang and Pei Xuan could only entreat them to accept the wine and fruit, but they refused even to taste it. The whole company proceeded to the water’s edge, where three warships from Liangshan Marsh lay waiting: one for the horses, one for Pei Xuan and the others, and one for the Grand Marshal and his entire retinue. The imperial edict and wine were first placed in the bow. That last vessel was under the command of Ruan Xiaoqi, the “Living King of Hell.”

p.src: That day Ruan Xiaoqi sat in the stern and assigned more than twenty stout men to row, each wearing a saber at his waist. When Grand Marshal Chen first boarded, he seated himself in the middle, haughty and overbearing, as though no one else were present. Ruan Xiaoqi called to the men, and as they set the vessel in motion, the boatmen on both sides began singing in unison. Equerry Li cursed them: “Country donkeys! A noble personage is present, yet you behave without the least restraint!” The boatmen paid him no heed and went on singing. Equerry Li picked up a rattan switch and struck at the boatmen on either side, but not one of them showed fear. Several of their leaders answered, “We are merely singing our own songs. What business is it of yours?” Equerry Li said, “You inexhaustible horde of rebels! How dare you answer me back?” He lashed out with the switch, and the boatmen on both sides all leaped into the water. From the stern Ruan Xiaoqi said, “You have beaten my boatmen until they jumped into the water. How is this vessel to go on now?” Just then, two swift boats came downstream to meet them. It turned out that Ruan Xiaoqi had already stored water in two compartments. When the boats behind drew near, he pulled out the plugs and shouted, “The boat is leaking!” Water immediately surged into the hold, and by the time they cried for rescue, it was already more than a foot deep. The two boats pulled alongside, and everyone hurriedly rescued Grand Marshal Chen and transferred him aboard. Everyone thought only of rowing their vessels away; no one had time to attend to the imperial wine or edict. The two swift boats went on ahead.

p.src: Ruan Xiaoqi called the boatmen back aboard. They bailed out the hold and wiped all the decking dry. Then he said, “Bring me a bottle of the imperial wine. I shall taste it first.” One boatman took a bottle from the carrying case, broke its seal, and handed it to Ruan Xiaoqi. Ruan Xiaoqi took it and caught its rich fragrance. Ruan Xiaoqi said, “It may be poisoned. I will play the fool and taste some first.” There was neither bowl nor dipper, so he drank straight from the bottle and drained it in one draught. After finishing the bottle, Ruan Xiaoqi said, “It has some flavor.” One bottle was hardly enough, so he fetched another and drained that in a single draught too. Once he had acquired the taste, he drank four bottles in succession. Then Ruan Xiaoqi said, “What are we to do now?” A boatman said, “There is a cask of common clear spirits in the stern.” Ruan Xiaoqi said, “Bring me the dipper used for bailing. I will let every one of you wet his lips.” He divided the six bottles of imperial wine among all the boatmen, who drank them up. They filled ten bottles with the coarse local clear spirits, tied the original seals back on, and returned them to the dragon-and-phoenix carrying cases. Then they rowed like the wind, caught up at Golden Sands Beach, and landed just in time.

p.src: Song Jiang and the others were all waiting there to welcome them. Amid fragrant flowers, lanterns, and candles, gongs rang, drums thundered, and all the music of the stronghold sounded at once. The imperial wine was arranged on tables, each borne by four men. The imperial edict was likewise carried upon a table. When Grand Marshal Chen came ashore, Song Jiang and the others received him and immediately bowed their heads to the ground. Song Jiang said, “I am but a petty branded clerk whose crimes reach to heaven. We have put Your Excellency to the indignity of coming here and have failed to receive you properly. I beg you to forgive our offense.” Equerry Li said, “The Grand Marshal is a great noble and minister of the imperial court, and he has come to grant you amnesty. This is no trifling matter! How could you send such a leaky boat, crewed by that ignorant country bandit? He very nearly cost this great noble his life!” Song Jiang replied, “We have plenty of sound vessels here. How would we dare use a leaky boat to carry Your Excellency?” Administrative Officer Zhang said, “The Grand Marshal’s robe is still wet. How dare you deny it!” Behind Song Jiang, the Five Tiger Generals stayed close at either side, while the Eight Valiant Cavalry Generals clustered before and behind. Seeing Equerry Li and Administrative Officer Zhang gesticulating and swaggering back and forth before Song Jiang, they all longed to kill the pair; only their regard for Song Jiang restrained them from striking.

p.src: That day Song Jiang invited the Grand Marshal to mount the sedan chair so that the edict might be formally read, but it took four or five entreaties before he consented to enter it. Two horses were led over for Administrative Officer Zhang and Equerry Li to ride. Those two wretches, old enough to know better, put on the most insufferable airs. Only after Song Jiang had pleaded with them did they mount and set out. He ordered the company to sound drums and wind instruments in a great clamor as they escorted the party through the three passes. Song Jiang and the other hundred-odd leaders all followed behind. They escorted the party directly to the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness, where everyone dismounted and invited the Grand Marshal into the hall. The imperial wine and edict box were placed at the front. Grand Marshal Chen, Administrative Officer Zhang, and Equerry Li stood to the left, while Xiao Rang and Pei Xuan stood to the right. p.src: The edict proclaimed: Civil arts can bring peace to the realm, and martial might can secure the state. The Five Emperors relied on rites and music to establish their domains, while the Three Sovereigns used war and punishment to pacify the world. Affairs may proceed through obedience or rebellion, and men may be worthy or foolish. We have inherited the great enterprise of Our ancestors and spread abroad the radiance of the sun and moon; beneath the whole of heaven, none fails to submit as Our subject. Of late, you, Song Jiang, and your fellows have gathered as outlaws in the hills and forests and plundered prefectures and towns. We had intended to display Heaven's chastisement against you, but truly feared burdening Our people. We now dispatch Grand Commandant Chen Zongshan to offer you amnesty. On the day this edict arrives, surrender to the authorities all money, provisions, weapons, horses, and boats in your possession, demolish your stronghold, and lead your men to the capital; your former crimes shall be pardoned. Should you remain blind to conscience and defy the imperial command, once Heaven's army arrives, not even a child shedding its milk teeth shall be spared. This edict is therefore issued for your full understanding. Proclaimed by imperial edict on a day in the fourth month, the first month of summer, in the third year of Xuanhe.

p.src: No sooner had Xiao Rang finished reading than Song Jiang and all those below him showed anger on their faces. Suddenly Li Kui, the Black Whirlwind, leapt down from the rafters, snatched the edict from Xiao Rang's hands, tore it to shreds, then seized Grand Commandant Chen and raised his fist to strike him. Song Jiang and Lu Junyi threw themselves across him and held him fast, refusing to let him strike. They had only just pulled them apart when Adjutant Li shouted, “Who is this scoundrel, to show such brazen insolence?” Li Kui had been itching for someone to hit. He grabbed Adjutant Li by the head and began beating him, shouting, “Who said the words written in this edict?” Secretary Zhang stammered, “It...is...His Majesty's sacred command.” Li Kui said, “That emperor of yours knows nothing of the many heroes here! He comes to offer us lords amnesty, yet puts on such airs! Your emperor's surname is Song, and my elder brother's surname is Song too. If he can be emperor, why should my elder brother alone be unable to become emperor? Do not provoke your black daddy, or one way or another I'll kill every official who drafted that edict!” Everyone came to restrain and admonish him, and they pushed the Black Whirlwind out of the hall.

p.src: Song Jiang said, “Set your mind at ease, Grand Commandant. Not the slightest harm shall come to you. Now bring out the imperial wine, so that everyone may partake of His Majesty's favor.” They immediately brought a set of jeweled golden-flowered goblets, and Song Jiang ordered Pei Xuan to take one jar of imperial wine and pour it into the great silver wine bowl. When they looked, however, it was merely rustic white liquor. They opened the other nine jars and poured them all into the bowl, but each contained the same thin rustic brew. At the sight, everyone was appalled, and one after another they left the hall. Lu Zhishen raised his iron禅 staff and cursed at the top of his voice, “Mother-begotten bastards! This is an intolerable insult! They pass off watery swill as imperial wine to fool us into drinking it!” Liu Tang, the Red-Haired Devil, charged forward brandishing his broad-bladed sword; Wu Song, the Pilgrim, drew his twin戒 swords; and Mu Hong the Unrestrained and Shi Jin the Nine-Tattooed Dragon erupted as well. The six naval commanders went down toward the passes, cursing all the way.

p.src: Seeing that matters had gone too far, Song Jiang placed himself in the midst of the men to hold them back. He urgently issued an order to have sedan chairs and horses escort the Grand Commandant down the mountain and permit no one to harm him. By then, more than half of all the commanders, high and low, had joined the uproar. Song Jiang and Lu Junyi had no choice but to mount in person and escort the Grand Commandant and all those who had come to proclaim the edict beyond the three passes. Bowing twice, they pleaded guilty: “It is not that we, Song Jiang and the others, lack the will to submit. The officials who drafted the edict simply do not understand the circumstances that drove us to Liangshan Marsh. Had they comforted us with a few kindly words, we would have devoted ourselves loyally to the state and died ten thousand deaths without regret. When you return to court, Grand Commandant, please speak kindly on our behalf.” They hurriedly escorted them across the ferry. Terrified out of their wits, the entire party fled at full speed to Jizhou.

p.src: Now Song Jiang returned to the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness and gathered the commanders once more at the banquet. Song Jiang said, “Though the court's edict was ill-conceived, all of you were far too hot-tempered.” Wu Yong said, “Elder brother, cease this blind persistence! The day for amnesty will come when it comes. How can you blame our brothers for losing their tempers? The court shows far too little regard for men! Put all idle talk aside now, elder brother, and issue orders: have the cavalry saddle and ready their horses, the infantry prepare their weapons, and the navy set their boats in order. Sooner or later a great army is certain to come against us. Let us annihilate them in one or two battles, leaving men and horses strewn dead and not a shred of armor to return. Once even their dreams are filled with fear of us, we can discuss the matter again.” Everyone said, “The military adviser speaks most rightly.” The banquet ended that day, and each man returned to his own quarters.

p.src: Meanwhile, Grand Commandant Chen returned to Jizhou and related to Zhang Shuye everything that had happened when the edict was proclaimed at Liangshan Marsh. Zhang Shuye asked, “Could it be that you said something excessive to them?” Grand Commandant Chen replied, “When did I ever dare utter a single word?” Zhang Shuye said, “If that is so, all our efforts have been wasted and the affair ruined. You must hurry back to the capital, Grand Commandant, and report it to His Majesty. There is no time to lose.”

p.src: Grand Commandant Chen, Secretary Zhang, Adjutant Li, and their party traveled through the night back to the capital. They met Grand Preceptor Cai and gave a full account of how the bandits of Liangshan Marsh had torn up and reviled the edict. Cai Jing flew into a rage on hearing this. “How dare these grass bandits behave with such insolence! How can the august Song dynasty permit the likes of you to run rampant?” Grand Commandant Chen wept, “Were it not for the protection of Your Excellency's good fortune, this humble official's bones would have been ground to dust at Liangshan Marsh! Today I have escaped from death and lived to see my gracious patron again!” The Grand Preceptor immediately sent invitations to Privy Commissioner Tong and the two Grand Commandants Gao and Yang, asking them to come to his residence to deliberate on this grave military matter. Before long, they had all arrived at the White Tiger Hall in the Grand Preceptor's residence. After the officials were seated, Grand Preceptor Cai summoned Secretary Zhang and Adjutant Li and had them recount in full how the Liangshan bandits had torn up and reviled the edict. Grand Commandant Yang said, “How could anyone have advocated granting amnesty to these bandits? Which official proposed it in the first place?” Grand Commandant Gao said, “Had I been at court that day, I would certainly have stopped it. How could I ever have allowed such a thing to proceed?” Privy Commissioner Tong said, “What cause is there to fear such petty thieves and curs? Though I possess little talent, I shall personally lead an army, set a fixed date, sweep the marsh clean, and return.” The officials said, “We shall report this tomorrow.” They then dispersed.

p.src: At court early the next morning, the officials cried “Long live the Emperor” three times. When the rites between sovereign and ministers were complete, Grand Preceptor Cai stepped from the ranks and reported the affair to the Son of Heaven. The Son of Heaven was furious and asked, “Who was it that urged Us that day to offer them amnesty?” An attending minister, a Secretariat Drafter, reported, “It was Censor-in-Chief Cui Jing who proposed it that day.” The Son of Heaven ordered Cui Jing seized and delivered to the Court of Judicial Review for trial. The Son of Heaven then asked Cai Jing, “These bandits have wrought havoc for a long while. Whom can We send to suppress them?” Grand Preceptor Cai replied, “They cannot be subdued without a powerful army. In my humble opinion, an official of the Privy Council must personally lead a great force to exterminate them; then victory may be won by a fixed date.” The Son of Heaven summoned Privy Commissioner Tong Guan and asked, “Will you lead troops to capture the outlaws of Liangshan Marsh?” Tong Guan knelt and replied, “The ancients said, ‘In filial duty one must exert all one's strength; in loyalty one must give one's life.’ I am willing to render the service of a hound or horse and remove this mortal threat to Your Majesty.” Gao Qiu and Yang Jian both endorsed him as well.

p.src: The Son of Heaven immediately issued a sacred command, bestowed on Tong Guan a golden seal and military tally, and appointed the Privy Commissioner of the Eastern Hall commander-in-chief. He was authorized to select and mobilize troops from every quarter, march against the bandits of Liangshan Marsh, and set an auspicious day for departure. Upon the commander's terrace he bares his arms and calls himself marshal; defeated in battle, he knits his brows like a child. How Privy Commissioner Tong marched to war will be told in the next chapter.
